    def plot_cindex_forest(
    self,
    cox_df: Optional[pd.DataFrame] = None,
    ax: Optional[plt.Axes] = None,
    title: Optional[str] = None,
    original_name: Optional[str] = None,
    figsize: Tuple[float, float] = (6, 6),
) -> Tuple[plt.Figure, pd.DataFrame]:
    """
    Forest plot of the C-index of every synthetic dataset with its confidence interval.

    The grey band is the confidence interval of the reference C-index, the solid line its
    point value and the dashed line C = 0.5 (no survival signal). A red cross marks a
    hazard ratio on the opposite side of 1 from the reference (reversed association).

    Args:
        cox_df (Optional[pd.DataFrame]): Output of :meth:`compute_cox_metrics`; computed
            with default settings when None and not computed before.
        ax (Optional[matplotlib.axes.Axes]): Target axis; a new figure when None.
        title (Optional[str]): Panel title; defaults to the endpoint and reference C-index.
        original_name (Optional[str]): Reference dataset; defaults to self.original_name.
        figsize (tuple[float, float]): Figure size when a new figure is created.

    Returns:
        tuple[matplotlib.figure.Figure, pd.DataFrame]: (figure, table plotted).
    """
    if cox_df is None:
        cox_df = self.cox_df
    if cox_df is None:
        cox_df = self.compute_cox_metrics(original_name=original_name)
    ref_name = original_name or self.original_name

    if ax is None:
        fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=figsize)
    else:
        fig = ax.figure

    ref = cox_df[cox_df["Dataset"] == ref_name].iloc[0]
    syn = cox_df[cox_df["Dataset"] != ref_name].reset_index(drop=True)

    if pd.notna(ref["CI_low"]):
        ax.axvspan(ref["CI_low"], ref["CI_high"], color="#bdbdbd", alpha=0.45, lw=0, zorder=0)
    if pd.notna(ref["C-index"]):
        ax.axvline(ref["C-index"], color="#4d4d4d", lw=1.4, zorder=1)
    ax.axvline(0.5, color="#d32f2f", lw=1.1, ls="--", zorder=1)

    x_lo, x_hi = 0.3, 0.9
    for i, r in syn.iterrows():
        y = -i
        color = self.dataset_colors.get(str(r["Dataset"]), "#8c8c8c")
        if pd.isna(r["C-index"]):
            ax.text(x_lo + 0.02, y, "N/A", ha="left", va="center", fontsize=7, color="#9e9e9e",
                    style="italic")
            continue
        if pd.notna(r["CI_low"]):
            ax.plot([r["CI_low"], r["CI_high"]], [y, y], color=color, lw=1.6, zorder=2)
        if r["HR_same_direction"] == 0:
            ax.plot(r["C-index"], y, marker="X", ms=8, mfc="#d32f2f", mec="white", mew=0.6,
                    zorder=3, ls="none")
        else:
            ax.plot(r["C-index"], y, marker="o", ms=5.5, mfc=color, mec="black", mew=0.7,
                    zorder=3, ls="none")

    ax.set_yticks([-i for i in range(len(syn))])
    ax.set_yticklabels(syn["Dataset"].astype(str), fontsize=9)
    ax.tick_params(axis="y", length=0)
    ax.set_ylim(-len(syn) + 0.4, 0.6)
    ax.set_xlim(x_lo, x_hi)
    ax.grid(axis="x", alpha=0.3, ls=":", lw=0.6)
    ax.spines[["top", "right"]].set_visible(False)
    ax.set_xlabel(f"C-index ({self._ci_label(cox_df)} CI)", fontsize=10)
    if title is None:
        title = f"{self.time_target}; {ref_name} C = {ref['C-index']:.2f}"
        if pd.notna(ref["CI_low"]):
            title += f" ({ref['CI_low']:.2f}–{ref['CI_high']:.2f})"
    ax.set_title(title, fontsize=10)

    handles = [
        plt.Line2D([], [], marker="o", ls="none", mfc="#bdbdbd", mec="black", ms=5.5,
                   label="Synthetic dataset"),
        plt.Line2D([], [], marker="X", ls="none", mfc="#d32f2f", mec="white", ms=8,
                   label="HR opposite to the reference"),
        mpatches.Patch(color="#bdbdbd", alpha=0.45, label=f"{ref_name} C-index CI"),
        plt.Line2D([], [], color="#d32f2f", ls="--", label="C = 0.5"),
    ]
    ax.legend(handles=handles, loc="upper center", bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, -0.16), ncol=2,
              fontsize=7, frameon=False)
    return fig, cox_df

    def plot_grid(
    self,
    figsize: Optional[Tuple[float, float]] = (18, 6),
    show_censors: bool = True,
    ci_show: bool = False,
    title_prefix: Optional[str] = "Survival",
    dataset_strip_height: float = 0.02,
    dataset_strip_y: float = 1.01,
    save_dir: Optional[str] = None
) -> Tuple[plt.Figure, pd.DataFrame]:
    """
    Plot a manuscript-style grid of Kaplan–Meier survival curves for all datasets.

    Args:
        figsize (Tuple[float, float], optional): Figure dimensions (W, H).
        show_censors (bool): Whether to display censor marks.
        ci_show (bool): Whether to render CI for KM curves.
        title_prefix (str, optional): Prefix for subplot titles.
        dataset_strip_height (float): Height of colored dataset strip.
        dataset_strip_y (float): Y-position of top dataset strip.
        save_dir (str, optional): If set, save individual dataset KM curves to this folder.

    Returns:
        Tuple[plt.Figure, pd.DataFrame]: The matplotlib Figure and the summary dataframe.

    Raises:
        None
    """
    import scienceplots  # noqa: F401  (registers the "science" matplotlib styles)

    plt.style.use(["science", "nature", "notebook"])
    plt.rcParams.update({
        "font.size": 10 * self.font_scale,
        "axes.titlesize": 11 * self.font_scale,
        "axes.labelsize": 10 * self.font_scale,
        "legend.fontsize": 9 * self.font_scale,
        "xtick.labelsize": 9 * self.font_scale,
        "ytick.labelsize": 9 * self.font_scale,
        "axes.linewidth": 1.0,
        "text.usetex": False,
        "axes.edgecolor": "#333333",
        "xtick.minor.visible": False,
        "ytick.minor.visible": False,
        "xtick.top": False,
        "ytick.right": False,
    })
    fig = plt.figure(figsize=figsize)
    gs = gridspec.GridSpec(2, 4, figure=fig, wspace=0.1, hspace=0.3,
                           width_ratios=[2, 1.25, 1.25, 1.25], height_ratios=[1, 1])
    ax_origin = fig.add_subplot(gs[:, 0])
    ax_origin.set_box_aspect(1)
    axes_small = []
    for r in range(2):
        for c in range(1, 4):
            ax = fig.add_subplot(gs[r, c])
            axes_small.append(ax)
    max_small_axes = len(axes_small)
    synthetic_names = [d for d in self.dataset_names if d != self.original_name]
    color_A = self.group_colors.get("GroupA", "#0072B2")
    color_B = self.group_colors.get("GroupB", "#D55E00")

    def _plot_single(ds_name: str, ax: plt.Axes, is_large: bool = False, save: bool = False) -> None:
        """
        Plot KM curve for a single dataset.

        Args:
            ds_name (str): Dataset name.
            ax (plt.Axes): Matplotlib axes.
            is_large (bool): If True, use larger annotation and legend.
            save (bool): If True, save individual plot.

        Returns:
            None
        """
        df_raw = self.datasets_dict[ds_name].copy()
        df = df_raw.copy()
        df[self.event_target] = pd.to_numeric(df.get(self.event_target, 0), errors="coerce").fillna(0).astype(int)
        df[self.time_target] = pd.to_numeric(df.get(self.time_target, np.nan), errors="coerce")
        df_A = df[df[self.phenotype_column] == self.value_A].copy()
        df_B = df[df[self.phenotype_column] == self.value_B].copy()
        n_A, n_B = len(df_A), len(df_B)
        ds_color = self.dataset_colors.get(ds_name, "#cccccc")
        ax.add_patch(
            plt.Rectangle(
                (0, dataset_strip_y),
                1,
                dataset_strip_height,
                transform=ax.transAxes,
                facecolor=ds_color,
                edgecolor="none",
                clip_on=False,
                zorder=10,
            )
        )
        kmf = KaplanMeierFitter()
        plotted_any = False
        for group_df, label, group_color in [
            (df_B, f"{self.value_B} (n={n_B})", color_B),
            (df_A, f"{self.value_A} (n={n_A})", color_A),
        ]:
            if len(group_df) == 0 or not group_df[self.time_target].notna().any():
                continue
            g = group_df.dropna(subset=[self.time_target, self.event_target])
            if len(g) == 0:
                continue
            kmf.fit(g[self.time_target], event_observed=g[self.event_target], label=label)
            kmf.plot_survival_function(
                ax=ax,
                ci_show=ci_show,
                show_censors=show_censors,
                color=group_color,
                linewidth=2.0 if is_large else 1.8,
                censor_styles={"ms": 4, "marker": "|", "mew": 1.2} if show_censors else None,
            )
            plotted_any = True
        # Annotations
        pvalue = self.summary_df.loc[self.summary_df["Dataset"] == ds_name, "pvalue"].values[0] \
            if self.summary_df is not None else np.nan
        cindex_text = self.summary_df.loc[self.summary_df["Dataset"] == ds_name, "C-index"].values[0] \
            if self.summary_df is not None else "NA"
        ptext = "p = NA" if (pvalue is None or np.isnan(pvalue)) else f"p = {pvalue:.4g}"
        ax.text(
            0.98, 0.96, ptext, transform=ax.transAxes,
            fontsize=10 * self.font_scale,
            horizontalalignment="right", verticalalignment="top", zorder=10,
        )
        ax.text(
            0.98, 0.88, f"C-index: {cindex_text}", transform=ax.transAxes,
            fontsize=10 * self.font_scale,
            horizontalalignment="right", verticalalignment="top", zorder=10,
        )
        title_t = f"{ds_name}" if title_prefix is None else f"{title_prefix}: {ds_name}"
        ax.set_title(title_t, fontweight="bold", pad=12)
        ax.set_xlabel(f"Time ({self.time_target})")
        ax.set_ylabel("Survival probability" if is_large else "")
        ax.set_ylim(0, 1.02)
        ax.grid(True, axis="y", linestyle="--", linewidth=0.6, alpha=0.5)
        if plotted_any:
            ax.legend(
                frameon=True, framealpha=1.0, loc="lower left",
                bbox_to_anchor=(0, 0.02), borderaxespad=0.2,
            )
        else:
            ax.text(
                0.5, 0.5, "No valid survival data",
                ha="center", va="center", transform=ax.transAxes,
                fontsize=11 * self.font_scale,
            )
            leg = ax.get_legend()
            if leg is not None:
                leg.remove()
        if save and save_dir:
            fig_indiv = plt.figure(figsize=(6, 5))
            ax_indiv = fig_indiv.add_subplot(111)
            _plot_single(ds_name, ax_indiv, is_large=True, save=False)
            fig_indiv.tight_layout()
            if self.is_pdf:
                outpath = os.path.join(save_dir, f"{ds_name}_KMcurve.pdf")
            else: 
                outpath = os.path.join(save_dir, f"{ds_name}_KMcurve.png")
            fig_indiv.savefig(outpath, dpi=300)
            plt.close(fig_indiv)

    _plot_single(self.original_name, ax_origin, is_large=True, save=bool(save_dir))
    for i, ds_name in enumerate(synthetic_names):
        if i >= max_small_axes:
            break
        _plot_single(ds_name, axes_small[i], is_large=False, save=bool(save_dir))
    for j in range(len(synthetic_names), max_small_axes):
        axes_small[j].axis("off")
    plt.tight_layout()
    return fig, self.summary_df

    @dataclass
class BayesianComparison:
    """
    Compute Bayesian pairwise comparisons using the external baycomp package and plot heatmaps.

    Args:
        rope (float): ROPE threshold for practical equivalence.
        seed (int): Random seed for reproducibility in baycomp.
        style (BaycompStyle): Plot styling settings for consistent manuscript figures.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If rope is not positive.
    """
    rope: float = 0.01
    seed: int = 0
    style: BaycompStyle = BaycompStyle()

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        if self.rope <= 0:
            raise ValueError("rope must be > 0.")

    @staticmethod
    def _validate_scores(scores: Sequence[float], method: str) -> np.ndarray:
        """
        Validate and coerce a score sequence to a finite numpy array.

        Args:
            scores (Sequence[float]): Metric values across repeated runs (seeds/folds).
            method (str): Method name for error messages.

        Returns:
            np.ndarray: Finite float numpy array of scores.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If fewer than 2 finite scores are present.
        """
        x = np.asarray(scores, dtype=float)
        x = x[np.isfinite(x)]
        if x.size < 2:
            raise ValueError(f"Method '{method}' must have at least 2 finite scores for baycomp.")
        return x

    @staticmethod
    def _resolve_methods_order(
        method_to_scores: Mapping[str, Sequence[float]],
        methods_order: Optional[Sequence[str]],
    ) -> List[str]:
        """
        Resolve and validate the method ordering.

        Args:
            method_to_scores (Mapping[str, Sequence[float]]): Mapping method -> scores.
            methods_order (Optional[Sequence[str]]): Optional explicit ordering.

        Returns:
            List[str]: Ordered list of methods.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If fewer than 2 methods are provided.
            ValueError: If methods_order contains methods not present in method_to_scores.
        """
        if not method_to_scores or len(method_to_scores) < 2:
            raise ValueError("method_to_scores must contain at least 2 methods.")

        if methods_order is None:
            return list(method_to_scores.keys())

        resolved = list(methods_order)
        missing = [m for m in resolved if m not in method_to_scores]
        if missing:
            raise ValueError(f"methods_order contains methods missing in method_to_scores: {missing}")
        return resolved

    def compare_methods(
        self,
        method_to_scores: Mapping[str, Sequence[float]],
        methods_order: Optional[Sequence[str]] = None,
    ) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """
        Compute ordered-pair Bayesian comparison probabilities for a set of methods.

        Args:
            method_to_scores (Mapping[str, Sequence[float]]): Mapping method -> scores across seeds/folds.
            methods_order (Optional[Sequence[str]]): Optional ordering for methods.

        Returns:
            pd.DataFrame: Table with columns:
                ["Method 1", "Method 2", "Better Prob", "Worse Prob", "Equivalent Prob"].

        Raises:
            ValueError: If fewer than 2 methods are provided.
            ValueError: If any method has fewer than 2 finite scores.
        """
        methods = self._resolve_methods_order(method_to_scores, methods_order)
        scores_np = {m: self._validate_scores(method_to_scores[m], method=m) for m in methods}

        rows: List[dict] = []
        for i, m1 in enumerate(methods):
            for j, m2 in enumerate(methods):
                if i == j:
                    continue

                p_left, p_rope, p_right = baycomp.two_on_single(
                    scores_np[m1],
                    scores_np[m2],
                    rope=self.rope,
                    plot=False,
                )

                rows.append(
                    {
                        "Method 1": m1,
                        "Method 2": m2,
                        "Better Prob": float(p_left),
                        "Worse Prob": float(p_right),
                        "Equivalent Prob": float(p_rope),
                    }
                )

        return pd.DataFrame(rows)

    @staticmethod
    def comparison_to_matrix(
        comparison_df: pd.DataFrame,
        methods_order: Sequence[str],
        value_col: str = "Better Prob",
        nan_diagonal: bool = True,
    ) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """
        Convert a comparison table into a square matrix suitable for heatmap plotting.

        Args:
            comparison_df (pd.DataFrame): Output of compare_methods.
            methods_order (Sequence[str]): Method ordering for rows and columns.
            value_col (str): Which column to visualize.
            nan_diagonal (bool): If True, set diagonal values to NaN.

        Returns:
            pd.DataFrame: Square matrix with index=Method 1 and columns=Method 2.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If value_col is not present in comparison_df.
        """
        if value_col not in comparison_df.columns:
            raise ValueError(f"value_col must be a column in comparison_df, got '{value_col}'.")

        mat = comparison_df.pivot(index="Method 1", columns="Method 2", values=value_col)
        mat = mat.reindex(index=list(methods_order), columns=list(methods_order))

        if nan_diagonal:
            for m in methods_order:
                if m in mat.index and m in mat.columns:
                    mat.loc[m, m] = np.nan

        return mat

    def plot_pbetter_heatmap_grid(
        self,
        cancer_to_method_scores: Mapping[str, Mapping[str, Sequence[float]]],
        cancers_order: Sequence[str] = ("ccRCC", "Melanoma", "NSCLC"),
        methods_order: Optional[Sequence[str]] = None,
        value_col: str = "Better Prob",
        figsize: Tuple[float, float] = (18, 5),
        annot: bool = True,
        fmt: str = ".2f",
        missing_hatch: str = "///",
        show: bool = True,
    ) -> Tuple[plt.Figure, np.ndarray, Dict[str, pd.DataFrame], Dict[str, pd.DataFrame]]:
        """
        Plot a 1xN grid of baycomp probability heatmaps (one per cancer).

        Args:
            cancer_to_method_scores (Mapping[str, Mapping[str, Sequence[float]]]): Cancer -> method/tool -> score list.
            cancers_order (Sequence[str]): Order of cancers in the grid.
            methods_order (Optional[Sequence[str]]): Global method ordering. If None, uses union across cancers.
            value_col (str): Which probability to visualize:
                "Better Prob", "Worse Prob", or "Equivalent Prob".
            figsize (Tuple[float, float]): Figure size.
            annot (bool): If True, annotate cells (NaN cells are blank).
            fmt (str): Annotation format.
            missing_hatch (str): Hatch pattern for missing (NaN) cells.
            show (bool): If True, calls plt.show().

        Returns:
            Tuple[plt.Figure, np.ndarray, Dict[str, pd.DataFrame], Dict[str, pd.DataFrame]]: Tuple containing:
                - fig: Matplotlib Figure object.
                - axes: Array of Axes objects.
                - matrices_by_cancer: Probability matrices for each cancer.
                - comparison_dfs_by_cancer: Comparison DataFrames for each cancer.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If value_col is invalid.
            ValueError: If any requested cancer is missing from cancer_to_method_scores.
            ValueError: If resolved methods_order is empty.
        """
        allowed = {"Better Prob", "Worse Prob", "Equivalent Prob"}
        if value_col not in allowed:
            raise ValueError(f"value_col must be one of {sorted(allowed)}.")

        cancers = list(cancers_order)
        for c in cancers:
            if c not in cancer_to_method_scores:
                raise ValueError(f"Cancer '{c}' missing from cancer_to_method_scores.")

        if methods_order is None:
            union_methods: List[str] = []
            for c in cancers:
                for m in cancer_to_method_scores[c].keys():
                    if m not in union_methods:
                        union_methods.append(m)
            methods_order_resolved = union_methods
        else:
            methods_order_resolved = list(methods_order)

        if len(methods_order_resolved) == 0:
            raise ValueError("methods_order resolved to an empty list.")

        _set_nature_rcparams(fontsize=self.style.fontsize)
        sns.set(style="white", rc={"axes.facecolor": self.style.plot_colors["heatmap_bg"]})

        fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, len(cancers), figsize=figsize)
        if len(cancers) == 1:
            axes = np.array([axes])

        norm = TwoSlopeNorm(vmin=0.0, vcenter=0.5, vmax=1.0)
        cmap = self.style.pbetter_cmap if value_col == "Better Prob" else plt.get_cmap("viridis")

        matrices_by_cancer: Dict[str, pd.DataFrame] = {}
        comparison_by_cancer: Dict[str, pd.DataFrame] = {}

        for ax, cancer in zip(axes, cancers):
            present_methods = set(cancer_to_method_scores[cancer].keys())

            comp_df = build_baycomp_comparison_df(
                method_to_scores=cancer_to_method_scores[cancer],
                methods_order=methods_order_resolved,
                rope=self.rope,
            )
            comparison_by_cancer[cancer] = comp_df

            mat = pd.DataFrame(index=methods_order_resolved, columns=methods_order_resolved, dtype=float)
            if not comp_df.empty:
                mat_present = comp_df.pivot(index="Method 1", columns="Method 2", values=value_col)
                mat.loc[mat_present.index, mat_present.columns] = mat_present

            for m in methods_order_resolved:
                if m in present_methods:
                    mat.loc[m, m] = 0.5

            matrices_by_cancer[cancer] = mat

            mask = mat.isna()
            sns.heatmap(
                mat,
                ax=ax,
                cmap=cmap,
                norm=norm if value_col == "Better Prob" else None,
                mask=mask,
                annot=annot,
                fmt=fmt,
                linewidths=0.5,
                linecolor="lightgray",
                cbar=(ax is axes[-1]),
                cbar_kws={"label": value_col} if (ax is axes[-1]) else None,
                square=True,
            )

            _overlay_hatched_missing_cells(
                ax=ax,
                mat=mat,
                hatch=missing_hatch,
                edgecolor=self.style.plot_colors.get("missing_edge", STABILITY_PLOT_COLORS["missing_edge"]),
                facecolor=self.style.plot_colors.get("missing_face", STABILITY_PLOT_COLORS["missing_face"]),
                linewidth=0.6,
            )

            for i, m in enumerate(methods_order_resolved):
                if m in present_methods:
                    rect = mpatches.Rectangle(
                        (i, i),
                        1.0,
                        1.0,
                        facecolor="#D3D3D3",
                        edgecolor="lightgray",
                        linewidth=0.5,
                        zorder=11,
                    )
                    ax.add_patch(rect)

            ax.set_title(cancer, fontsize=self.style.fontsize + 1, fontweight="bold", pad=10)

            cancer_color = self.style.cancer_colors.get(cancer, "#333333")
            ax.plot(
                [0.02, 0.98],
                [1.02, 1.02],
                transform=ax.transAxes,
                color=cancer_color,
                lw=4,
                clip_on=False,
            )

            ax.set_xlabel("Method 2", fontsize=self.style.fontsize)
            ax.set_ylabel("Method 1", fontsize=self.style.fontsize)
            plt.setp(ax.get_xticklabels(), rotation=45, ha="right", rotation_mode="anchor")
            ax.tick_params(axis="y", rotation=0)

        plt.tight_layout()
        if show:
            plt.show()

        return fig, axes, matrices_by_cancer, comparison_by_cancer

    @staticmethod
def comparison_to_matrix(
    comparison_df: pd.DataFrame,
    methods_order: Sequence[str],
    value_col: str = "Better Prob",
    nan_diagonal: bool = True,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """
    Convert a comparison table into a square matrix suitable for heatmap plotting.

    Args:
        comparison_df (pd.DataFrame): Output of compare_methods.
        methods_order (Sequence[str]): Method ordering for rows and columns.
        value_col (str): Which column to visualize.
        nan_diagonal (bool): If True, set diagonal values to NaN.

    Returns:
        pd.DataFrame: Square matrix with index=Method 1 and columns=Method 2.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If value_col is not present in comparison_df.
    """
    if value_col not in comparison_df.columns:
        raise ValueError(f"value_col must be a column in comparison_df, got '{value_col}'.")

    mat = comparison_df.pivot(index="Method 1", columns="Method 2", values=value_col)
    mat = mat.reindex(index=list(methods_order), columns=list(methods_order))

    if nan_diagonal:
        for m in methods_order:
            if m in mat.index and m in mat.columns:
                mat.loc[m, m] = np.nan

    return mat

    def plot_pbetter_heatmap_grid(
    self,
    cancer_to_method_scores: Mapping[str, Mapping[str, Sequence[float]]],
    cancers_order: Sequence[str] = ("ccRCC", "Melanoma", "NSCLC"),
    methods_order: Optional[Sequence[str]] = None,
    value_col: str = "Better Prob",
    figsize: Tuple[float, float] = (18, 5),
    annot: bool = True,
    fmt: str = ".2f",
    missing_hatch: str = "///",
    show: bool = True,
) -> Tuple[plt.Figure, np.ndarray, Dict[str, pd.DataFrame], Dict[str, pd.DataFrame]]:
    """
    Plot a 1xN grid of baycomp probability heatmaps (one per cancer).

    Args:
        cancer_to_method_scores (Mapping[str, Mapping[str, Sequence[float]]]): Cancer -> method/tool -> score list.
        cancers_order (Sequence[str]): Order of cancers in the grid.
        methods_order (Optional[Sequence[str]]): Global method ordering. If None, uses union across cancers.
        value_col (str): Which probability to visualize:
            "Better Prob", "Worse Prob", or "Equivalent Prob".
        figsize (Tuple[float, float]): Figure size.
        annot (bool): If True, annotate cells (NaN cells are blank).
        fmt (str): Annotation format.
        missing_hatch (str): Hatch pattern for missing (NaN) cells.
        show (bool): If True, calls plt.show().

    Returns:
        Tuple[plt.Figure, np.ndarray, Dict[str, pd.DataFrame], Dict[str, pd.DataFrame]]: Tuple containing:
            - fig: Matplotlib Figure object.
            - axes: Array of Axes objects.
            - matrices_by_cancer: Probability matrices for each cancer.
            - comparison_dfs_by_cancer: Comparison DataFrames for each cancer.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If value_col is invalid.
        ValueError: If any requested cancer is missing from cancer_to_method_scores.
        ValueError: If resolved methods_order is empty.
    """
    allowed = {"Better Prob", "Worse Prob", "Equivalent Prob"}
    if value_col not in allowed:
        raise ValueError(f"value_col must be one of {sorted(allowed)}.")

    cancers = list(cancers_order)
    for c in cancers:
        if c not in cancer_to_method_scores:
            raise ValueError(f"Cancer '{c}' missing from cancer_to_method_scores.")

    if methods_order is None:
        union_methods: List[str] = []
        for c in cancers:
            for m in cancer_to_method_scores[c].keys():
                if m not in union_methods:
                    union_methods.append(m)
        methods_order_resolved = union_methods
    else:
        methods_order_resolved = list(methods_order)

    if len(methods_order_resolved) == 0:
        raise ValueError("methods_order resolved to an empty list.")

    _set_nature_rcparams(fontsize=self.style.fontsize)
    sns.set(style="white", rc={"axes.facecolor": self.style.plot_colors["heatmap_bg"]})

    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, len(cancers), figsize=figsize)
    if len(cancers) == 1:
        axes = np.array([axes])

    norm = TwoSlopeNorm(vmin=0.0, vcenter=0.5, vmax=1.0)
    cmap = self.style.pbetter_cmap if value_col == "Better Prob" else plt.get_cmap("viridis")

    matrices_by_cancer: Dict[str, pd.DataFrame] = {}
    comparison_by_cancer: Dict[str, pd.DataFrame] = {}

    for ax, cancer in zip(axes, cancers):
        present_methods = set(cancer_to_method_scores[cancer].keys())

        comp_df = build_baycomp_comparison_df(
            method_to_scores=cancer_to_method_scores[cancer],
            methods_order=methods_order_resolved,
            rope=self.rope,
        )
        comparison_by_cancer[cancer] = comp_df

        mat = pd.DataFrame(index=methods_order_resolved, columns=methods_order_resolved, dtype=float)
        if not comp_df.empty:
            mat_present = comp_df.pivot(index="Method 1", columns="Method 2", values=value_col)
            mat.loc[mat_present.index, mat_present.columns] = mat_present

        for m in methods_order_resolved:
            if m in present_methods:
                mat.loc[m, m] = 0.5

        matrices_by_cancer[cancer] = mat

        mask = mat.isna()
        sns.heatmap(
            mat,
            ax=ax,
            cmap=cmap,
            norm=norm if value_col == "Better Prob" else None,
            mask=mask,
            annot=annot,
            fmt=fmt,
            linewidths=0.5,
            linecolor="lightgray",
            cbar=(ax is axes[-1]),
            cbar_kws={"label": value_col} if (ax is axes[-1]) else None,
            square=True,
        )

        _overlay_hatched_missing_cells(
            ax=ax,
            mat=mat,
            hatch=missing_hatch,
            edgecolor=self.style.plot_colors.get("missing_edge", STABILITY_PLOT_COLORS["missing_edge"]),
            facecolor=self.style.plot_colors.get("missing_face", STABILITY_PLOT_COLORS["missing_face"]),
            linewidth=0.6,
        )

        for i, m in enumerate(methods_order_resolved):
            if m in present_methods:
                rect = mpatches.Rectangle(
                    (i, i),
                    1.0,
                    1.0,
                    facecolor="#D3D3D3",
                    edgecolor="lightgray",
                    linewidth=0.5,
                    zorder=11,
                )
                ax.add_patch(rect)

        ax.set_title(cancer, fontsize=self.style.fontsize + 1, fontweight="bold", pad=10)

        cancer_color = self.style.cancer_colors.get(cancer, "#333333")
        ax.plot(
            [0.02, 0.98],
            [1.02, 1.02],
            transform=ax.transAxes,
            color=cancer_color,
            lw=4,
            clip_on=False,
        )

        ax.set_xlabel("Method 2", fontsize=self.style.fontsize)
        ax.set_ylabel("Method 1", fontsize=self.style.fontsize)
        plt.setp(ax.get_xticklabels(), rotation=45, ha="right", rotation_mode="anchor")
        ax.tick_params(axis="y", rotation=0)

    plt.tight_layout()
    if show:
        plt.show()

    return fig, axes, matrices_by_cancer, comparison_by_cancer

    def build_baycomp_comparison_df(
    method_to_scores: Mapping[str, Sequence[float]],
    methods_order: Optional[Sequence[str]] = None,
    rope: float = 0.01,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """
    Compute pairwise Bayesian comparison probabilities (better/worse/equivalent)
    using baycomp.two_on_single for all ordered pairs of methods.

    Args:
        method_to_scores (Mapping[str, Sequence[float]]): Mapping tool/method -> list/array of scores.
        methods_order (Optional[Sequence[str]]): Optional method ordering. If None, uses dict keys.
        rope (float): ROPE threshold for practical equivalence.

    Returns:
        pd.DataFrame: Comparison table with columns:
            ["Method 1", "Method 2", "Better Prob", "Worse Prob", "Equivalent Prob"].

    Raises:
        ValueError: If rope is not positive.
        ValueError: If fewer than 2 methods are provided.
        ValueError: If any method has fewer than 2 finite scores.
    """
    if rope <= 0:
        raise ValueError("rope must be > 0.")

    if not method_to_scores or len(method_to_scores) < 2:
        raise ValueError("method_to_scores must contain at least 2 methods.")

    methods = list(method_to_scores.keys()) if methods_order is None else list(methods_order)

    scores_np: Dict[str, np.ndarray] = {}
    for m in methods:
        if m not in method_to_scores:
            continue
        x = np.asarray(method_to_scores[m], dtype=float)
        x = x[np.isfinite(x)]
        if x.size < 2:
            raise ValueError(f"Method '{m}' must have at least 2 finite scores for baycomp.")
        scores_np[m] = x

    present_methods = [m for m in methods if m in scores_np]
    if len(present_methods) < 2:
        raise ValueError("Fewer than 2 methods remain after filtering invalid scores / missing methods.")

    rows: List[dict] = []
    for m1 in present_methods:
        for m2 in present_methods:
            if m1 == m2:
                continue

            p_left, p_rope, p_right = baycomp.two_on_single(
                scores_np[m1],
                scores_np[m2],
                rope=rope,
                plot=False,
            )

            rows.append(
                {
                    "Method 1": m1,
                    "Method 2": m2,
                    "Better Prob": float(p_left),
                    "Worse Prob": float(p_right),
                    "Equivalent Prob": float(p_rope),
                }
            )

    return pd.DataFrame(rows)

    Metrics: Privacy¶

    The metrics.privacy module provides tools to assess the likelihood of privacy attacks using synthetic data.

    singling_out ¶

    Singling-out risk evaluation for synthetic data.

    Provides helper functions that wrap the singling-out evaluator of Anonymeter, in the polars implementation used for the SynOmicsBench results (vendored under synomicsbench.third_party.anonymeter_polars; the pandas evaluator of Anonymeter is too slow on cohorts with tens of thousands of columns), to run univariate and multivariate singling-out attacks.

    With a control dataset (patients from the same population that the generator never saw), the evaluators report the residual risk (R_attack - R_control) / (1 - R_control); without it, the attack risk is compared with the naive (random-guess) baseline. See :func:synomicsbench.metrics.privacy.risk.privacy_risk_table.

    def eval_singling_out_multivariate(
    ori: pd.DataFrame,
    syns: Dict[str, pd.DataFrame],
    n_cols_list: Sequence[int] = (2, 3, 5, 7, 10, 20, 50),
    n_attacks: int = 10_000,
    max_attempts: int = 1_000_000,
    seed: int = 42,
    control: Optional[pd.DataFrame] = None,
    evaluator_seed: Optional[int] = None,
) -> Dict[str, List[SinglingOutEvaluator]]:
    """Run multivariate singling-out attacks at varying attribute-combination sizes.

    The predicates are drawn from all columns of ``ori``.

    Args:
        ori: Original dataset.
        syns: Mapping from synthetic dataset name to its DataFrame.
        n_cols_list: Number of columns the attacker uses per predicate.
        n_attacks: Number of attack predicates per evaluation.
        max_attempts: Maximum predicate generation attempts.
        seed: Seed of the predicate generation.
        control: Optional dataset of patients not used to train the generators, with the
            columns of ``ori``; enables the residual risk.
        evaluator_seed: Seed of the predicate generation in place of ``seed``, as in
            :func:`eval_singling_out_univariate`.

    Returns:
        Mapping from synthetic dataset name to a list of evaluated
        ``SinglingOutEvaluator`` instances (one per ``n_cols`` value).
    """
    results: Dict[str, List[SinglingOutEvaluator]] = {}

    for syn_name, syn_df in syns.items():
        o, s, c = subset_frames(ori, syn_df, control, ori.columns)
        risks: List[SinglingOutEvaluator] = []
        for n_col in n_cols_list:
            evaluator = SinglingOutEvaluator(
                ori=o,
                syn=s,
                n_cols=n_col,
                n_attacks=n_attacks,
                max_attempts=max_attempts,
                seed=seed if evaluator_seed is None else evaluator_seed,
                control=c,
            )
            evaluator.evaluate(mode="multivariate")
            risks.append(evaluator)
        results[syn_name] = risks

    return results

    def eval_singling_out_univariate(
    ori: pd.DataFrame,
    syns: Dict[str, pd.DataFrame],
    n_attacks: int = 10_000,
    max_attempts: int = 1_000_000,
    proportions: Sequence[float] = (1.0,),
    seed: int = 42,
    control: Optional[pd.DataFrame] = None,
    clinical_cols: ColumnSpec = None,
    transcriptomic_cols: ColumnSpec = None,
    gene_sets: GeneSetSpec = None,
    evaluator_seed: Optional[int] = None,
) -> Dict[str, List[SinglingOutEvaluator]]:
    """Run univariate singling-out attacks at several attacker knowledge levels.

    Each knowledge level is a set of columns the attacker knows: all ``clinical_cols``
    plus a named gene set or a fraction of the genes (see
    :func:`synomicsbench.metrics.privacy.knowledge.knowledge_levels`). Without
    ``clinical_cols``, the fractions are taken over all columns.

    Args:
        ori: Original (real) dataset after post-processing.
        syns: Mapping from synthetic dataset name to its DataFrame.
        n_attacks: Number of attack predicates to generate per evaluation.
        max_attempts: Maximum predicate generation attempts.
        proportions: Fractions of the genes (of all columns without ``clinical_cols``)
            known by the attacker.
        seed: Seed of the gene sampling (reset at every knowledge level).
        control: Optional dataset of patients not used to train the generators, with the
            columns of ``ori``; enables the residual risk.
        clinical_cols: Clinical columns (names or positions), known at every level.
        transcriptomic_cols: Gene columns; ``None`` uses every non-clinical column.
        gene_sets: Optional named gene sets evaluated before the fractions: a path to a
            ``.gmt`` file or a mapping such as ``{"FGES": [...]}``.
        evaluator_seed: Seed of the predicate generation; ``None`` uses ``seed``.
            SynOmicsBench used the seed of each synthetic dataset.

    Returns:
        Mapping from synthetic dataset name to a list of evaluated
        ``SinglingOutEvaluator`` instances, one per knowledge level (gene sets first,
        then ``proportions``).
    """
    clinical, genes = resolve_columns(ori.columns, clinical_cols, transcriptomic_cols)
    levels = knowledge_levels(clinical, genes, proportions, gene_sets, seed)

    results: Dict[str, List[SinglingOutEvaluator]] = {}
    for syn_name, syn_df in syns.items():
        risks: List[SinglingOutEvaluator] = []
        for _, cols in levels:
            o, s, c = subset_frames(ori, syn_df, control, cols)
            evaluator = SinglingOutEvaluator(
                ori=o,
                syn=s,
                n_attacks=n_attacks,
                n_cols=1,
                max_attempts=max_attempts,
                seed=seed if evaluator_seed is None else evaluator_seed,
                control=c,
            )
            evaluator.evaluate(mode="univariate")
            risks.append(evaluator)
        results[syn_name] = risks

    return results

    linkability ¶

    Linkability risk evaluation for synthetic data.

    Evaluates whether an attacker can use synthetic data to link molecular (gene expression) profiles to clinical attributes of the same individual.

    eval_linkability_genes_clinical(ori, syns, clinical_cols, transcriptomic_cols=None, n_neighbors=1, proportions=(1.0,), seed=42, control=None, gene_sets=None, evaluator_seed=None) ¶

    Evaluate linkability risk between gene expression and clinical features.

    The attack attempts to link two disjoint attribute sets of the same patient (the clinical variables, and the genes of one knowledge level) using the synthetic dataset as a bridge.

    Parameters:

    		 required

    List of column names or integer indices for transcriptomic (gene) features. If None, uses all remaining columns not in clinical_cols.

    		 None
    n_neighbors int

    Number of nearest neighbors for the linkability attack.

    def eval_linkability_genes_clinical(
    ori: pd.DataFrame,
    syns: Dict[str, pd.DataFrame],
    clinical_cols: ColumnSpec,
    transcriptomic_cols: ColumnSpec = None,
    n_neighbors: int = 1,
    proportions: Sequence[float] = (1.0,),
    seed: int = 42,
    control: Optional[pd.DataFrame] = None,
    gene_sets: GeneSetSpec = None,
    evaluator_seed: Optional[int] = None,
) -> Dict[str, List[LinkabilityEvaluator]]:
    """Evaluate linkability risk between gene expression and clinical features.

    The attack attempts to link two disjoint attribute sets of the same
    patient (the clinical variables, and the genes of one knowledge level) using the
    synthetic dataset as a bridge.

    Args:
        ori: Original dataset.
        syns: Mapping from synthetic dataset name to its DataFrame.
        clinical_cols: List of column names or integer indices for clinical
            features. If indices are provided, they refer to ``ori`` column
            positions.
        transcriptomic_cols: List of column names or integer indices for
            transcriptomic (gene) features. If ``None``, uses all remaining
            columns not in ``clinical_cols``.
        n_neighbors: Number of nearest neighbors for the linkability attack.
        proportions: Fractions of gene columns known by the attacker.
        seed: Seed of the gene sampling (reset at every knowledge level).
        control: Optional dataset of patients not used to train the generators, with the
            columns of ``ori``; enables the residual risk. The number of attacks is then
            bounded by its size.
        gene_sets: Optional named gene sets evaluated before the fractions: a path to a
            ``.gmt`` file or a mapping such as ``{"FGES": [...]}``.
        evaluator_seed: Seed of the draw of the target records, set before every
            evaluation; ``None`` uses ``seed``. It matters when ``control`` has fewer
            records than ``ori``, so that only part of the original records are attacked.

    Returns:
        Mapping from dataset name to a list of evaluated
        ``LinkabilityEvaluator`` instances, one per knowledge level (gene sets first,
        then ``proportions``).
    """
    clinical, genes = resolve_columns(ori.columns, clinical_cols, transcriptomic_cols)
    levels = knowledge_levels(clinical, genes, proportions, gene_sets, seed)
    n_attacks = n_record_attacks(ori, control)

    results: Dict[str, List[LinkabilityEvaluator]] = {}
    for syn_name, syn_df in syns.items():
        risks: List[LinkabilityEvaluator] = []
        for _, cols in levels:
            o, s, c = subset_frames(ori, syn_df, control, cols)
            evaluator = LinkabilityEvaluator(
                ori=o,
                syn=s,
                n_attacks=n_attacks,
                aux_cols=(clinical, cols[len(clinical):]),
                n_neighbors=n_neighbors,
                control=c,
            )
            with numpy_seed(seed if evaluator_seed is None else evaluator_seed):
                evaluator.evaluate(n_jobs=-2)
            risks.append(evaluator)
        results[syn_name] = risks

    return results

    def eval_inference_genes_clinical(
    ori: pd.DataFrame,
    syns: Dict[str, pd.DataFrame],
    clinical_cols: ColumnSpec,
    transcriptomic_cols: ColumnSpec = None,
    proportions: Sequence[float] = (1.0,),
    seed: int = 42,
    control: Optional[pd.DataFrame] = None,
    gene_sets: GeneSetSpec = None,
    evaluator_seed: Optional[int] = None,
) -> Dict[str, List[Tuple[str, str, object]]]:
    """Evaluate attribute inference risk for each clinical variable at several knowledge levels.

    Each knowledge level is a set of genes the attacker knows: a named gene set or a
    fraction of ``transcriptomic_cols`` (see
    :func:`synomicsbench.metrics.privacy.knowledge.knowledge_levels`). At every level and
    for every synthetic dataset, each clinical feature is in turn the *secret*: the
    ``InferenceEvaluator`` from Anonymeter predicts it from the known genes.

    Args:
        ori: Original dataset.
        syns: Mapping from synthetic dataset name to its DataFrame.
        clinical_cols: List of column names or integer indices for clinical
            features (secrets). If indices are provided, they refer to
            ``ori`` column positions.
        transcriptomic_cols: List of column names or integer indices for
            transcriptomic (gene) features (auxiliary). If ``None``, uses
            all remaining columns not in ``clinical_cols``.
        proportions: Fractions of the genes known by the attacker.
        seed: Seed of the gene sampling (reset at every knowledge level).
        control: Optional dataset of patients not used to train the generators, with the
            columns of ``ori``; enables the residual risk. The number of attacks is then
            bounded by its size.
        gene_sets: Optional named gene sets evaluated before the fractions: a path to a
            ``.gmt`` file or a mapping such as ``{"FGES": [...]}``.
        evaluator_seed: Seed of the draw of the target records and of the naive guesses,
            set before every evaluation; ``None`` uses ``seed``.

    Returns:
        Mapping from dataset name to a list of ``(level, secret, results)`` tuples, one
        per knowledge level (gene sets first, then ``proportions``) and secret, where
        ``results`` is an ``EvaluationResults`` object or an error dict if the evaluation
        failed.
    """
    clinical, genes = resolve_columns(ori.columns, clinical_cols, transcriptomic_cols)
    levels = knowledge_levels(clinical, genes, proportions, gene_sets, seed)
    n_attacks = n_record_attacks(ori, control)

    results_all: Dict[str, List[Tuple[str, str, object]]] = {}

    for tool, syn_data in syns.items():
        results: List[Tuple[str, str, object]] = []
        logger.info("Starting inference evaluation for %s", tool)

        for level, cols in levels:
            o, s, c = subset_frames(ori, syn_data, control, cols)
            known_genes = cols[len(clinical):]
            for secret in clinical:
                try:
                    evaluator = InferenceEvaluator(
                        ori=o,
                        syn=s,
                        aux_cols=known_genes,
                        secret=secret,
                        n_attacks=n_attacks,
                        control=c,
                    )
                    with numpy_seed(seed if evaluator_seed is None else evaluator_seed):
                        evaluator.evaluate(n_jobs=-2)
                    res = evaluator.results()
                    results.append((level, secret, res))
                    logger.info("Tool %s: level %s secret %s risk=%s", tool, level, secret,
                                res.risk().value)
                except Exception as ex:
                    logger.exception(
                        "Error evaluating tool=%s level=%s secret=%s: %s", tool, level, secret, ex
                    )
                    results.append((level, secret, {"error": str(ex)}))

        results_all[tool] = results

    return results_all

    knowledge ¶

    Attacker knowledge levels shared by the privacy attacks.

    An attacker is assumed to know the clinical attributes of a patient and part of the transcriptome. Each knowledge level is the list of columns the attack may use: all clinical columns, plus either a named gene set (e.g. a published signature) or a random fraction of the genes. Every fraction is drawn after resetting the same seed, so all synthetic datasets are attacked on exactly the same columns. Gene sets are given as a mapping or read from a .gmt file.

    FGES_GMT is the bundled .gmt file of the tumor microenvironment (TME)-related functional gene expression signatures (FGES) used by SynOmicsBench (Bagaev et al., 2021, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ccell.2021.04.014): gene_sets={"FGES": FGES_GMT} is one knowledge level with the genes of all these signatures.

    def knowledge_levels(
    clinical: Sequence[str],
    genes: Sequence[str],
    proportions: Sequence[float] = (1.0,),
    gene_sets: GeneSetSpec = None,
    feature_seed: int = 42,
) -> List[Tuple[str, List[str]]]:
    """Columns available to the attacker at each knowledge level.

    Named gene sets come first, in the order given, then the gene fractions. A gene set
    keeps the genes of ``genes`` it contains, in the order of ``genes``. A fraction ``p``
    below 1 draws ``int(p * len(genes))`` genes after ``random.seed(feature_seed)``.

    Args:
        clinical: Clinical columns, known at every level.
        genes: Gene columns the attacker may know.
        proportions: Fractions of ``genes`` known by the attacker.
        gene_sets: Optional named gene sets: a path to a ``.gmt`` file (one level per set)
            or a mapping such as ``{"panel": [...]}``. A mapping value that is a path to a
            ``.gmt`` file is one level with the genes of all its sets, e.g.
            ``{"FGES": FGES_GMT}``.
        feature_seed: Seed of the gene sampling.

    Returns:
        List of ``(label, columns)``; fractions are labelled like ``"25%"``.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If a gene set shares no gene with ``genes``.
    """
    clinical, genes = list(clinical), list(genes)
    levels: List[Tuple[str, List[str]]] = []

    if isinstance(gene_sets, (str, os.PathLike)):
        gene_sets = read_gmt(gene_sets)
    for name, members in (gene_sets or {}).items():
        if isinstance(members, (str, os.PathLike)):
            members = {g for genes in read_gmt(members).values() for g in genes}
        members = set(members)
        selected = [g for g in genes if g in members]
        if not selected:
            raise ValueError(f"Gene set '{name}' shares no gene with the attacked columns.")
        levels.append((str(name), clinical + selected))

    for p in proportions:
        if p >= 1.0:
            selected = list(genes)
        else:
            random.seed(feature_seed)
            selected = random.sample(genes, int(len(genes) * p))
        levels.append((level_label(p), clinical + selected))

    return levels

    def n_record_attacks(ori: pd.DataFrame, control: Optional[pd.DataFrame]) -> int:
    """Number of record-level attacks: every original record, bounded by the control size.

    Anonymeter attacks the same number of records in the original and the control dataset,
    sampling without replacement, so the smaller of the two bounds the attack budget.
    """
    return int(ori.shape[0] if control is None else min(ori.shape[0], control.shape[0]))

    numpy_seed(seed) ¶

    Seed numpy's global generator for the duration of one evaluation.

    Anonymeter's linkability and inference evaluators draw their target records (and the guesses of the naive attacker of inference) with DataFrame.sample, i.e. numpy's global generator: seeding it makes the evaluation repeatable. The previous state of the generator is restored afterwards. None leaves the generator as it is.

    @contextmanager
def numpy_seed(seed: Optional[int]) -> Iterator[None]:
    """Seed numpy's global generator for the duration of one evaluation.

    Anonymeter's linkability and inference evaluators draw their target records (and the
    guesses of the naive attacker of inference) with ``DataFrame.sample``, i.e. numpy's global
    generator: seeding it makes the evaluation repeatable. The previous state of the generator
    is restored afterwards. ``None`` leaves the generator as it is.
    """
    if seed is None:
        yield
        return
    state = np.random.get_state()
    np.random.seed(seed)
    try:
        yield
    finally:
        np.random.set_state(state)

    def read_gmt(path: Union[str, "os.PathLike[str]"]) -> Dict[str, List[str]]:
    """Read gene sets from a ``.gmt`` file.

    Each line holds a set name, a description and the member genes, separated by tabs.

    Args:
        path: Path to the ``.gmt`` file.

    Returns:
        Mapping from set name to member genes, in file order.
    """
    gene_sets: Dict[str, List[str]] = {}
    with open(path) as handle:
        for line in handle:
            fields = [f.strip() for f in line.rstrip("\n").split("\t")]
            if len(fields) < 3 or not fields[0]:
                continue
            gene_sets[fields[0]] = [g for g in fields[2:] if g]
    return gene_sets

    def resolve_columns(
    columns: Sequence[str],
    clinical_cols: ColumnSpec,
    transcriptomic_cols: ColumnSpec = None,
) -> Tuple[List[str], List[str]]:
    """Resolve clinical and transcriptomic column names.

    Args:
        columns: Columns of the original dataset.
        clinical_cols: Clinical column names or integer positions in ``columns``.
        transcriptomic_cols: Gene column names or positions; ``None`` uses every column
            that is not clinical.

    Returns:
        ``(clinical column names, gene column names)``, in the order given.
    """
    columns = list(columns)

    def _names(spec: ColumnSpec) -> List[str]:
        spec = list(spec) if spec is not None else []
        if spec and isinstance(spec[0], int):
            return [columns[i] for i in spec]
        return list(spec)

    clinical = _names(clinical_cols)
    if transcriptomic_cols is None:
        clinical_set = set(clinical)
        genes = [c for c in columns if c not in clinical_set]
    else:
        genes = _names(transcriptomic_cols)
    return clinical, genes

    def subset_frames(
    ori: pd.DataFrame,
    syn: pd.DataFrame,
    control: Optional[pd.DataFrame],
    cols: Sequence[str],
) -> Tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame, Optional[pd.DataFrame]]:
    """Restrict the original, synthetic and control datasets to the attacked columns.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If the synthetic or control dataset lacks some of the columns.
    """
    cols = list(cols)
    for name, df in (("synthetic", syn), ("control", control)):
        if df is None:
            continue
        missing = [c for c in cols if c not in df.columns]
        if missing:
            raise ValueError(
                f"The {name} dataset lacks {len(missing)} attacked column(s), e.g. {missing[:5]}. "
                "Reduce all datasets to the columns they share first."
            )
    return ori[cols], syn[cols], (None if control is None else control[cols])

    risk ¶

    Tidy risk tables from the privacy attack results.

    Every attack function of :mod:synomicsbench.metrics.privacy returns, per synthetic dataset, a list of evaluated Anonymeter evaluators (or (level, secret, results) tuples for attribute inference). :func:privacy_risk_table turns them into one row per evaluation.

    • With a control dataset, the reported risk is Anonymeter's residual risk R_residual = (R_attack - R_control) / (1 - R_control), bounded below by zero: the part of the attack's success that it would not also achieve on patients the generator never saw. R_attack and R_control are reported alongside.
    • Without a control dataset, the attack risk R_attack is reported with the risk of a naive attacker guessing at random, R_naive; an attack that does not beat it has failed.

    def privacy_risk_table(
    results: Mapping[str, Sequence[Any]],
    attack: str,
    configs: Optional[Sequence[str]] = None,
    confidence_level: float = 0.95,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """One row per evaluation of one attack family.

    Args:
        results: Output of one attack function, ``{dataset: [evaluator, ...]}`` or, for
            attribute inference, ``{dataset: [(level, secret, results), ...]}``.
        attack: Attack name written in the ``Attack`` column (e.g. ``"Singling out (univariate)"``).
        configs: Label of each evaluation in the lists, e.g. the knowledge levels
            (``["FGES", "25%", "100%"]``) or the ``n_cols`` values; defaults to the position
            in the list. Inference results carry their level (``Config``) and secret
            (``Secret`` column).
        confidence_level: Confidence level of the intervals.

    Returns:
        pd.DataFrame: Columns Dataset, Attack, Config (and Secret for inference), then the
        residual-risk columns
        (R_residual, its CI, R_attack, its CI, R_control) when the evaluations used a
        control dataset, otherwise R_attack, its CI and R_naive with its CI. Failed
        inference evaluations are left out.
    """
    rows: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
    for dataset, items in results.items():
        for i, item in enumerate(items):
            if isinstance(item, tuple):
                level, secret, item = item
                labels = {"Config": str(level), "Secret": str(secret)}
            else:
                labels = {"Config": str(configs[i]) if configs is not None else str(i)}
            if isinstance(item, dict):
                continue
            res = _results(item, confidence_level)
            rows.append({"Dataset": dataset, "Attack": attack, **labels, **risk_record(res)})

    table = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    if table.empty:
        return pd.DataFrame(columns=["Dataset", "Attack", "Config", *NAIVE_COLUMNS])
    risk_cols = RESIDUAL_COLUMNS if "R_residual" in table.columns else NAIVE_COLUMNS
    keys = [c for c in ("Dataset", "Attack", "Config", "Secret") if c in table.columns]
    extra = [c for c in table.columns if c not in risk_cols and c not in keys]
    return table[[*keys, *risk_cols, *extra]].replace({None: np.nan})

    def risk_record(res: Any) -> Dict[str, float]:
    """Risks of one evaluation (an Anonymeter ``EvaluationResults``).

    Returns:
        With a control set: R_residual (+ CI), R_attack (+ CI) and R_control.
        Without: R_attack (+ CI) and R_naive (+ CI).
    """
    attack = res.attack_rate.to_risk()
    row = {
        "R_attack": float(attack.value),
        "R_attack_ci_low": float(attack.ci[0]),
        "R_attack_ci_high": float(attack.ci[1]),
    }
    if res.control_rate is not None:
        residual = res.risk()
        row.update({
            "R_residual": float(residual.value),
            "R_residual_ci_low": float(residual.ci[0]),
            "R_residual_ci_high": float(residual.ci[1]),
            "R_control": float(res.control_rate.value),
        })
    else:
        naive = res.risk(baseline=True)
        row.update({
            "R_naive": float(naive.value),
            "R_naive_ci_low": float(naive.ci[0]),
            "R_naive_ci_high": float(naive.ci[1]),
        })
    return row

    @dataclass
class BenchmarkConfig:
    """Settings of the automatic benchmark. The defaults match the Melanoma cohort of SynOmicsBench.

    Args:
        id_column: Sample-ID column; used as the index when present.
        gene_start_column: First transcriptomic column. Used only when ``clinical_cols`` and
            ``transcriptomic_cols`` are not given: the columns before it are clinical, the
            others are genes.
        clinical_cols: Clinical columns (explicit partition, with ``transcriptomic_cols``).
        transcriptomic_cols: Gene columns (explicit partition, with ``clinical_cols``).
        metadata: Optional feature-type dict (``feature_metadata.json`` format) or path to it;
            its ``ordinal_categorical`` columns are treated as ordinal by the fidelity metrics.
        phenotype_source_col: Clinical column the two compared groups are derived from (DGE,
            GSEA, survival).
        responder_values: Values of ``phenotype_source_col`` of the first group.
        progressor_values: Values of ``phenotype_source_col`` of the second group.
        label_col: Name of the derived two-group column.
        label_values: Names of the two groups in ``label_col``.
        log_transform: The gene values are on a linear scale (e.g. TPM): transform them to
            log2(x + 1) before DGE, GSEA and network preservation.
        gene_set: ``.gmt`` file of GSEA and ssGSEA (default: the bundled MSigDB Hallmark sets).
        gsea_permutations: Permutations of the pre-ranked GSEA.
        survival_endpoints: ``(time_col, event_col)`` of each endpoint (e.g. OS and PFS); the
            survival score is their mean.
        corr_method: Correlation of the bivariate similarity.
        n_bins: Bins of the bivariate similarity of numerical-categorical pairs.
        threshold_unique_values: Columns with fewer unique values are categorical.
        fidelity_masking: Re-introduce the missing values recorded in ``missingindicator_*``
            columns before the fidelity metrics.
        clinical_ordinal_features: Ordinal clinical columns; ``None`` reads them from ``metadata``.
        network_n_genes: Most variable genes of the network.
        network_n_permutations: Permutations of the module preservation statistics.
        network_threads: Threads of WGCNA. The network settings are those of
            :class:`~synomicsbench.metrics.fidelity.NetworkPreservation.NetworkPreservation`
            (needs R with the WGCNA package).
        cibersortx: CIBERSORTx results (the only input computed outside the package): a
            directory with one CSV per dataset, or a mapping ``{"original": path, name: path}``,
            where ``name`` is the name of a synthetic dataset. In a directory, the files are
            ``<name>.csv`` or ``CIBERSORTx_<name>_Results.csv``, and the original data is
            ``original``, ``Original`` or ``Origin``.
        top_k_cell_types: Most abundant cell types (in the original data) used by the
            Aitchison distance.
        privacy_control: Optional control cohort (path or DataFrame): patients of the same
            population that the generators never saw. The privacy dimensions are then
            Anonymeter's residual risks; only the columns shared with the control are attacked.
        privacy_known_genes: Genes the attacker knows besides the clinical columns (default:
            all genes). The four attacks use these columns: inference infers each clinical
            column from the known genes.
        privacy_proportions: Fractions of the known genes held by the attacker in univariate
            singling out, linkability and inference: one evaluation per fraction, the genes of
            a fraction below 1 drawn with ``privacy_seed``. The risk is the mean over the levels.
        privacy_gene_sets: Optional named gene sets added as further levels, e.g.
            ``{"FGES": FGES_GMT}`` (see :func:`synomicsbench.metrics.privacy.knowledge.knowledge_levels`).
        privacy_n_attacks: Predicates of each singling-out attack.
        privacy_max_attempts: Maximum predicate generation attempts of singling out.
        privacy_so_multi_n_cols: Numbers of attributes combined in a multivariate
            singling-out predicate; the risk is the mean over these numbers.
        privacy_link_n_neighbors: Neighbours of the linkability attack.
        privacy_seed: Seed of the gene sampling of ``privacy_proportions``. The random draws
            of the four attacks on a synthetic dataset (singling-out predicates, target records
            of linkability and inference) use the seed of that dataset, so a run is repeatable.
        weights: Pillar weights (statistical fidelity, biological utility, privacy) of the
            meta-score (equal thirds by default). Pillars without a metric are left out and
            the other weights are rescaled to sum to 1.
        scenarios: Weighting scenarios of the sensitivity analysis, name -> weights; the
            report describes those of ``SCENARIO_DESCRIPTIONS``.
        collapse_dims: Dimensions whose values are averaged per method before ranking.
        on_error: ``"warn"`` records a failing metric in ``BenchmarkResult.errors`` and goes
            on; ``"raise"`` stops at the first failure.
        resume: Every metric is saved in ``output_dir/_work/values`` as soon as it is computed.
            With ``resume=True``, a run with the same inputs and settings reads the saved
            metrics back and computes only the missing ones (e.g. after a job was stopped).
        output_dir: Directory of the report and of the intermediate files.
        name_map: Display name -> file stem, used to name the methods parsed from file names.
        name_pattern: Regex parsing ``(method, seed)`` from a dataset name such as
            ``gaussiancopula_0``; without a trailing ``_<int>`` the dataset is a single seed.
    """

    # --- column layout ---
    id_column: str = "Patient"
    gene_start_column: str = "A1BG"
    clinical_cols: Optional[List[str]] = None
    transcriptomic_cols: Optional[List[str]] = None
    metadata: Optional[object] = None  # dict or path

    # --- phenotype split (DGE, GSEA, survival) ---
    phenotype_source_col: str = "BR"
    responder_values: Sequence[str] = ("CR", "PR")
    progressor_values: Sequence[str] = ("PD",)
    label_col: str = "Labels"
    label_values: Tuple[str, str] = ("Responder", "Progressor")

    # --- gene expression scale (DGE, GSEA, network) ---
    log_transform: bool = False

    # --- GSEA / ssGSEA ---
    gene_set: str = HALLMARK_GMT
    gsea_permutations: int = 10000

    # --- survival ---
    survival_endpoints: List[Tuple[str, str]] = field(
        default_factory=lambda: [("OS", "dead"), ("PFS", "progressed")]
    )

    # --- fidelity ---
    corr_method: str = "spearman"
    n_bins: int = 10
    threshold_unique_values: int = 10
    fidelity_masking: bool = True
    clinical_ordinal_features: Optional[List[str]] = None

    # --- network preservation ---
    network_n_genes: int = 10_000
    network_n_permutations: int = 200
    network_threads: int = 8

    # --- cell deconvolution ---
    cibersortx: Optional[Union[str, Dict[str, object]]] = None
    top_k_cell_types: int = 10

    # --- privacy ---
    privacy_control: Optional[object] = None  # path or DataFrame
    privacy_known_genes: Optional[List[str]] = None
    privacy_proportions: Tuple[float, ...] = (1.0,)
    privacy_gene_sets: Optional[object] = None  # .gmt path or {name: genes or .gmt path}
    privacy_n_attacks: int = 10_000
    privacy_max_attempts: int = 1_000_000
    privacy_so_multi_n_cols: Tuple[int, ...] = (2, 3, 5, 7, 10, 20, 50)
    privacy_link_n_neighbors: int = 1
    privacy_seed: int = 42

    # --- meta-score ---
    weights: Tuple[float, float, float] = (1 / 3, 1 / 3, 1 / 3)
    scenarios: Dict[str, Tuple[float, float, float]] = field(default_factory=lambda: dict(SCENARIOS))
    collapse_dims: Tuple[str, ...] = ()

    # --- run ---
    on_error: str = "warn"
    resume: bool = False
    output_dir: str = "autobenchmark_results"
    name_map: Dict[str, str] = field(default_factory=lambda: dict(NAME_MAP))
    name_pattern: str = r"(?P<method>.+)_(?P<seed>\d+)$"

    def __post_init__(self):
        if self.on_error not in ("warn", "raise"):
            raise ValueError(f"on_error must be 'warn' or 'raise', not '{self.on_error}'.")
        self.privacy_proportions = tuple(self.privacy_proportions)
        if not all(0 < p <= 1 for p in self.privacy_proportions):
            raise ValueError(f"privacy_proportions must be fractions in (0, 1], not {self.privacy_proportions}.")
        for name, w in [("weights", self.weights)] + [(f"scenario '{k}'", v) for k, v in self.scenarios.items()]:
            if len(w) != 3 or min(w) < 0 or sum(w) <= 0:
                raise ValueError(f"{name} must be three non-negative weights (statistical fidelity, "
                                 f"biological utility, privacy) with a positive sum, not {w}.")

    def ordinal_features(self, metadata: Optional[dict] = None) -> List[str]:
        """Ordinal clinical features of the fidelity metrics.

        Uses ``clinical_ordinal_features`` if set, otherwise the ``ordinal_categorical``
        entries of ``metadata``, otherwise none.
        """
        if self.clinical_ordinal_features is not None:
            return list(self.clinical_ordinal_features)
        if metadata:
            return [c for c, t in metadata.items() if t == "ordinal_categorical"]
        return []

    def resolve_columns(self, columns: Sequence[str]) -> Tuple[List[str], List[str]]:
        """Return (clinical_cols, transcriptomic_cols) for the given feature columns.

        Uses the explicit lists if provided, otherwise splits at ``gene_start_column``.
        The ``id_column`` is never included in either block.
        """
        cols = [c for c in columns if c != self.id_column]
        if self.clinical_cols is not None and self.transcriptomic_cols is not None:
            return list(self.clinical_cols), list(self.transcriptomic_cols)
        if self.gene_start_column not in cols:
            raise ValueError(
                f"gene_start_column '{self.gene_start_column}' is not a column of the data "
                f"(first columns: {cols[:5]}); set gene_start_column, or clinical_cols and "
                "transcriptomic_cols."
            )
        start = cols.index(self.gene_start_column)
        return cols[:start], cols[start:]

    @dataclass
class BenchmarkResult:
    """Outputs of a benchmark run.

    Attributes:
        per_dim_values: dimension -> long table [Model, Seed, Value].
        metascore: dimension -> {method: mean rank} (lower = better).
        value_table: method x dimension, mean value over the seeds.
        rank_table: method x dimension, mean rank.
        composite: weighted pillar scores and ``Total`` (the meta-score), lowest first.
        dims_run: dimensions computed.
        dims_missing: dimensions requested but not computed (see ``errors``).
        errors: dimension -> reason it was not computed.
        report_paths: files written by ``write_report`` (filled by :func:`run_benchmark`).
    """
    per_dim_values: Dict[str, pd.DataFrame]
    metascore: Dict[str, Dict[str, float]]
    value_table: pd.DataFrame
    rank_table: pd.DataFrame
    composite: Optional[pd.DataFrame] = None
    dims_run: List[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    dims_missing: List[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    errors: Dict[str, str] = field(default_factory=dict)
    report_paths: Dict[str, str] = field(default_factory=dict)

    @property
    def ranking(self) -> Optional[pd.Series]:
        """Meta-score of every method, best (lowest) first."""
        return None if self.composite is None else self.composite["Total"].sort_values()

    @property
    def report_html(self) -> Optional[str]:
        """Path of the HTML report, once written."""
        return self.report_paths.get("report_html")
